dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Ha! So Hertha's even roped our Honorary Knight into helping with this little venture?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: When we were discussing the drinks stand earlier, I took one look at the menu and could barely contain my excitement. Now it's finally time to sample the finished products.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I just had a couple of drinks at the plaza not long ago, but when it comes to fine wine, I'm a sucker for more... Ahem, as long as it stays within healthy limits, of course!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Now that I'm finally free to relax, it's time to start doing just that!

choices.text: I'm here as a willing employee this time!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Can't wait to see your skills in action! Give me something that goes well with casual conversation, but still packs a punch...

choices.text: Are you sure those requirements don't clash...?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Of course they don't clash!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: A drink that packs a punch means you have to drink it slowly... And if you want to chat, then it has to go down smooth... so, something with a sweet aftertaste. A conversational connoisseur requires the perfect balance...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: The most suitable choice on this menu would be the Thorny Lake. It's a drink with a real kick that you can find in almost every bar.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It's not enough to know the recipe, though — the key is in the mixing. Some bartenders choose to stick to the tried and tested basics, while others like to add their own personal flair.

choices.text: Alright, I'll give it my best shot!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That's the spirit! Now show me what you've got!

choices.text: I'll quickly learn the recipe and then give it a whirl!
Is this some sort of test?
I'm a hotshot mixologist, no matter how you look at it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here you go, Grand Master, a cocktail just for you! I guarantee you won't find this one too polite!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Such a spirited drink... How did you make this? That burning scent of Fire-Water... It's as if the very air were about to ignite! This is more like it!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Perfection! It's clear that once you let go of your inhibitions, your talents really shine through!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That first hit of Mint is like a cooling feint that masks the Fire-Water underneath.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: By the time the sweetness dissipates, the Fire-Water has already slipped in behind your guard, ready to deliver a powerful strike of intense flavor. It's exactly the impact I was hoping for!

choices.text: And that's topped off with a hint of Smetana...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That's the most ingenious part! Fire-Water's greatest flaw is a lack of aftertaste, but the Smetana perfectly maintains the flavor at the peak of its intensity!

choices.text: All this praise is making my cheeks red.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It's hard to imagine something this good was created by... a mixologist who doesn't even drink Fire-Water! I think it has the potential to become a firm favorite in Mondstadt and Nod-Krai!

choices.text: The Knight of Boreas's symbol is a wolf...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Iron Wolf... perfect! It's elegant yet wild. Only you could come up with such a fitting name!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I have an idea — why don't we name our Knights of Favonius' drinks stand after you? Let's call it "The Honorary Knight's Cocktail Shack"!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: No time to waste, I'll go have a word with Glenfidia right away!

choices.text: While the Knights of Favonius are as sturdy as iron...
So, how about calling this drink an "Iron Wolf"?
The real inspiration came from everything you said.
So the aftertaste won't feel too light...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Grand Master, I hereby present you with this Thorny Lake for your enjoyment and assessment!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, the color and aroma are certainly on point, but as for the balance of flavors... I'll just have to taste it and find out.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Not bad, you haven't overdone or skimped on any single ingredient... Though unfortunately, it's a little too "polite" for my tastes.

choices.text: Polite? How can a drink be polite?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Perhaps I should have said "modest"? You've followed the formula to a tee — but if anything, you've played it a little too safe.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Were you worried that deviating just a little might disappoint me?

choices.text: That's exactly what happened.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hey, we've fought side by side and dealt with things that even gods were loath to meddle with. Ours is a friendship forged in the margins between life and death!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That said, if you ask me, you can ditch the nerves and work your mixologist magic. I'm looking for something that shocks the senses!

choices.text: Alright, I'll get the creative juices flowing!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Mull it over, there's no rush! We can chat while you think — who knows, you might just find some inspiration to mix in with your magic!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Besides being too "polite," are there any other issues with my Thorny Lake?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Let me think... I guess you could say it lacks "impact." Even when following the same recipe, the techniques used to mix different ingredients can affect the taste.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Sometimes, deliberately creating layers between spirits can bring out the different "waves" as each one hits the taste buds in sequence.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: In this regard, too, you've taken quite a tentative approach. Why not be a little bolder?

choices.text: I think I understand...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, you catch on quickly. No need to explain further!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This massive tankard...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Pretty awesome, huh? It's like a hammer head that you can fill with wine when you're not using it to pound in nails!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It was a gift. Huffman came up with the idea, Charles supplied the design, Wagner helped cast it, and about ten or so knights chipped in to pay for the materials.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: They've been waiting to have a good drink with me, and this is my crucial "weapon" to aid me in a fair duel with them all.

choices.text: ...Fair?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'm the Grand Master, after all — I've been drinking a lot longer than them, I've practiced more assiduously, and I have a bit more meat to absorb the blows...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: So it's only fair to my subordinates that I drink a teensy bit more per round. Wouldn't you agree?

choices.text: That's a little more than just "teensy"...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Of course, some of them have been "training" as long as I have, and those ones won't be getting any special treatment.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Take Hazelnut 3 and Hazelnut 5, for example. Both were skilled warriors who helped me deal with Eroch back in the day. Nowadays, I have them helping Jean with miscellaneous duties.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: At today's after-work cool down, they insisted on trying to keep pace. In the end, they lost our game of darts and ended up passed out on the floor. Haha...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I've already told Jean that I won't be approving their leave requests for tomorrow, no matter what!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Drinking in a garden feels different from a tavern, right? Given the environment, why not try something with a floral twist?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ha, I like your style!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Speaking of this garden, it brings back memories of something that happened many years ago...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: When I was young, I liked to find Ruin Guards to test my fighting skills, both armed and unarmed. Once, I failed to take down a stray missile, and it ended up destroying a watchtower on the city walls...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: As punishment, I had to run fifty laps around the city, repair the watchtower, and help rebuild the shattered walls in this garden.

choices.text: Sounds like you caused quite the fuss...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Indeed, among the misadventures of my youth, this is one of the most memorable ones... Mostly because that day, Crepus saw me covered in dirt.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: He took two bottles of hundred-year-old wine and sent Diluc — who looked even younger than Mika does today — to work out a clever way to get rid of Feroux, who was guarding me.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It was so hot that day, I could swear I was about to pass out... On a whim, I picked some Mint leaves and put them in one of the wine bottles... and the result turned out to be surprisingly tasty.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: After Crepus tried it too, he was full of praise. He even wrote up an official recipe for my spontaneous creation.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: His customers loved it. Several summers passed, and Crepus kept writing letters about giving me a share of the profits... As though I could possibly accept!

choices.text: That must have been so long ago...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Yes... Good old Crepus.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: ...Feroux retired years ago, but he still gives me a stern stare every time we meet.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, he's a stubborn one. Diluc, who replaced him, and then Kaeya, who took over later, both performed impeccably. Changing times will always belong to the youth... He should have admitted defeat long ago!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: When I get the chance, I'll have Kaeya show him the amazing progress the Cavalry Company has made...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Anyway, on the subject of this garden, it's become a popular venue for hosting events.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It's a treasured place that the Knights of Favonius have maintained for years, so it makes sense that it's become the go-to location for organizing such things!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I heard that while the expedition was underway, you were a great help in giving those left behind the opportunity to put their energy to good use.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Sometimes, I look through the photos I've been given from those events — though unfortunately, there aren't enough to include everybody...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: My conclusion is that Mondstadt needs to do more to popularize the Kamera!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I wonder how these events might have turned out if you were here and not away on the expedition...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: If I were in charge of organizing events? Well... I suppose every one would revolve around fine wine, or at the very least, there would be some sort of tasting involved...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: For example, we could go all in on this drinks stand and open it to the whole city, with every company of the knights selecting one or more mixologists to compete against each other...

choices.text: I should have guessed...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, it's only a thought! Can't let things get too out of hand...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: If I were to actually throw a grand banquet, Jean would come after me with her sword drawn... Even Frederica would launch a punitive expedition!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: While in Nod-Krai, we had a rule that knights must never get drunk while at their posts. Otherwise, it could lead to dereliction of duty — with serious consequences.

choices.text: That sounds like a sensible rule.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Exactly. As expedition members return to their companies, my hope is that this rule will gradually spread to everyone in Mondstadt, too.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Just like Fire-Water and Smetana — these Nod-Krai delicacies have made their way into Mondstadt's households and become part of people's daily lives.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Young people need to learn restraint.

choices.text: I didn't know you had that side to you...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: At the end of the day, no one should be biting off more than they can chew...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Unless it's someone near my level, they shouldn't even be thinking about "enjoying a light buzz" when they've still got work to do. Most people would just end up a whole lot drunker than they'd like.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: You should come practice with me on weekends, haha! Trust me, once I've drunk them under the table, they'll be swearing off wine for a whole week!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What is it people say — "don't believe in fables"...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The good news is, I think I know what to make for you! Can I borrow your "hammer," please?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Huh? Oh, feel free!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Whatever you're about to do, I've got a feeling I've hit the jackpot...

choices.text: The fabled seasoned drinker's self-control...
Fun shouldn't get in the way of important matters.
That's exactly your style!
Long before I came to Mondstadt...
It's hard to imagine you getting disciplined so severely...
I think you may have got your handicaps the wrong way round...
...Duel?
I didn't pay enough attention to these details before...
Thanks to your encouragement, I'm ready to go all out!
I didn't want to disappoint the expert.
Is this some sort of riddle?
